'''Asier Illarramendi '''"'''Illarra'''" '''Andonegi ''' ({{IPA|es|aˈsjeɾ iʎaraˈmendi iˈʎara andoˈneɣi}}; born 8 March 1990) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Hong Kong Premier League]] club [[Kitchee SC|Kitchee]]. 

He developed at [[Real Sociedad]], helping them to qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] in [[2012–13 La Liga|2013]]. He then transferred to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for €32.2 million, the most they had ever paid for a Spanish player, returning to his first club for half of that fee two years later.

Illarramendi earned 31 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] from [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17]] to [[Spain national under-23 football team|under-23 level]], winning the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2013 European Championship]] with the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 side]]. He made his senior debut in 2017.

==Club career==
===Real Sociedad===
A product of local [[Real Sociedad]]'s youth system, Illarramendi was born in [[Mutriku]], [[Gipuzkoa]], and he spent the vast majority of his first four senior seasons with [[Real Sociedad B|the B team]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/noticias/2010-06-16/zubieta-garantiza-futuro-prometedor-20100616.html|title=Zubieta garantiza un futuro prometedor|trans-title=Zubieta guarantees a promising future|newspaper=[[El Diario Vasco]]|first=Miguel|last=González|language=es|date=16 June 2010|access-date=21 December 2017}}</ref> contributing 27 games and two goals in [[2009–10 Tercera División|2009–10]] as the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basques]] returned to [[Segunda División B]] after one year out. On 19 June 2010, in the last day of the [[Segunda División]] campaign, as the first team had already [[2009–10 Segunda División|sealed promotion]] to [[La Liga]] as champions, he made his first official appearance, in a 4–1 away loss against [[Elche CF]].<ref name=MD>{{cite news|url=https://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2010/06/20/pagina-45/5714551/pdf.html|title=Jorge Molina marca los cuatro goles y acaba 'pichichi' de la división de plata|trans-title=Jorge Molina scores all four goals to end silver division 'pichichi'|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=J.C.|last=Romero|language=es|date=20 June 2010|access-date=7 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/noticias/2010-06-20/illarra-albistegi-20100620.html|title=Ojo a Illarra y a Albistegi|trans-title=Keep your eye on Illarra and Albistegi|newspaper=El Diario Vasco|language=es|date=20 June 2010|access-date=28 February 2011}}</ref>

On 23 January 2011, Illarramendi made his top-division debut, in a 2–1 defeat at [[Villarreal CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302137?cc=5739|title=Rossi shines in Yellow Submarine victory|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=23 January 2011|access-date=28 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024055749/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302137?cc=5739|archive-date=24 October 2012}}</ref> The following month, he first appeared as a starter and played the full 90 minutes in another away loss (4–1 to [[RCD Espanyol]]);<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301856?cc=5739|title=Espanyol rally to beat Real|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=2 March 2011|access-date=3 May 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302122128/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301856?cc=5739|archive-date=2 March 2011}}</ref> the bulk of [[2010–11 Segunda División B|the season]] was spent, however, with the reserves in the third tier.

Illarramendi started in all of his 32 league appearances in [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13]], as Real Sociedad finished fourth and [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|qualified]] for the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in ten years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vivafutbol.es/realsociedad/noticias/6617-la-real-sociedad-tampoco-falla-ante-el-sevilla-fc|title=La Real Sociedad tampoco falla ante el Sevilla F.C.|trans-title=Real Sociedad do not fail against Sevilla F.C. as well|publisher=Viva Fútbol|language=es|date=19 May 2013|access-date=8 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130620094737/http://www.vivafutbol.es/realsociedad/noticias/6617-la-real-sociedad-tampoco-falla-ante-el-sevilla-fc|archive-date=20 June 2013}}</ref> At the [[La Liga Awards|LFP Awards]], he was named Breakthrough Player and Best Midfielder.<ref name=LFP>{{cite web|url=http://www.ligabbva.com/2544_liga-bbva/2321580_messi-mejor-delantero-y-mejor-jugador-cristiano-jugador-mas-valioso.html|title=Messi, mejor delantero y mejor jugador; Cristiano, jugador más valioso|trans-title=Messi, best forward and best player; Cristiano, most valuable player|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=2 December 2013|access-date=20 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721233232/http://www.ligabbva.com/2544_liga-bbva/2321580_messi-mejor-delantero-y-mejor-jugador-cristiano-jugador-mas-valioso.html|archive-date=21 July 2015}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Asier Illarramendi 2 (cropped).JPG|thumb|left|200px|Illarramendi in 2013]]
On 12 July 2013, Illarramendi signed a six-year contract with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for a fee of [[Euro|€]]32.2 million,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2013/07/12/4112360/real-madrid-reveal-3219-million-illarra-fee?ICID=CP_124|title=Real Madrid reveal €32.19 million Illarra fee|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=12 July 2013|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref> the highest amount paid by the club for a Spanish player.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2013/07/12/futbol/1373653968.html|title=Producto nacional a precio 'galáctico'|trans-title=National product at 'galactic' prices|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Carlos|last=Garcés Izquierdo|language=es|date=13 July 2013|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref> He made his official debut on 14 September by starting in a 2–2 away draw against Villarreal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/en/report/373182/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null|title=Bale's debut goal not enough|publisher=ESPN FC|date=14 September 2013|access-date=19 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131223130841/http://espnfc.com/en/report/373182/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null|archive-date=23 December 2013}}</ref> and scored his first goal on 18 December in a 2–0 home win over [[CD Olímpic de Xàtiva]] in the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|round of 32]] of the [[Copa del Rey]] (also the aggregate score).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/copa/dieciseisavos/vuelta/rma_olc/|title=El Madrid cumple con su tarea|trans-title=Madrid do their job|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=18 December 2013|access-date=19 December 2013}}</ref>

Illarramendi scored his first league goal for the ''Merengues'' on 22 February 2014, after his long-range effort against Elche was deflected and the hosts won 3–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_25/rma_elc/|title=Pleno sin Cristiano|trans-title=Three for three without Cristiano|newspaper=Marca|first=Santiago|last=Siguero|language=es|date=22 February 2014|access-date=5 April 2014}}</ref> His second came on 5 April, when he opened an eventual 4–0 victory at his former team Real Sociedad in the 44th minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_32/rso_rma/|title=El Madrid sigue al rebote|trans-title=Madrid still on the rebound|newspaper=Marca|first=Santiago|last=Siguero|language=es|date=5 April 2014|access-date=5 April 2014}}</ref> He was a regular in the domestic cup campaign, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Ángel Di María]] in the [[2014 Copa del Rey final|2–1 final defeat]] of [[FC Barcelona]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/10771036/Real-Madrid-2-Barcelona-1-Copa-del-Rey-final-report-Gareth-Bale-winner.html|title=Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 1, Copa del Rey final: match report as Gareth Bale scores wonder winner|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|first=Jim|last=White|date=17 April 2014|access-date=20 June 2015}}</ref> adding 11 matches – five starts – in the team's [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League run]] but remaining on the bench as they clinched the trophy against [[Atlético Madrid]] in [[2014 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] at the [[Estádio da Luz]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/05/22/futbol/champions_league/final-champions/1400756242.html|title=Illarra, de Mutriku a Lisboa|trans-title=Illarra, from Mutriku to Lisbon|newspaper=Marca|first=Santiago|last=Siguero|language=es|date=23 May 2014|access-date=16 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27383593|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Atlético Madrid|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Phil|last=McNulty|date=24 May 2014|access-date=16 June 2023}}</ref>

Illarramendi began his [[2014–15 La Liga|second year]] with a brief substitute appearance in the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup]] triumph against compatriots [[Sevilla FC]] at the [[Cardiff City Stadium]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28741099|title=Super Cup: Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice in Real Madrid win|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Rob|last=Phillips|date=12 August 2014|access-date=13 August 2014}}</ref> and was also part of Real Madrid's squad which [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|won]] the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] in Morocco, playing the entirety of the 4–0 semi-final win over [[Cruz Azul]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30470531|title=Cruz Azul 0–4 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 December 2014|access-date=20 June 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Real Sociedad===
[[File:FC Salzburg gegen Real Sociedad San Sebastian (22. Februar 2018, EL Sechzehntelfinale) 31.jpg|thumb|Illarramendi in 2018]]
On 26 August 2015, Illarramendi returned to Real Sociedad, signing a six-year deal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realsociedad.com/document/view/spa/225/190657/la-real-ficha-a-illarra|title=La Real ficha a Illarra|trans-title=Real sign Illarra|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/official-announcement-illarramendi|title=Official announcement: Illarramendi|publisher=Real Madrid|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref>– the transfer fee was not officially disclosed by the clubs, but was stated in the media as being between €15–17 million, around half of the figure paid in the opposite direction two years previously.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/diarioas/2015/08/26/english/1440582260_270177.html|title=Illarra arrives in San Sebastián to complete La Real move|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|date=26 August 2015|access-date=31 January 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150828223724/https://as.com/diarioas/2015/08/26/english/1440582260_270177.html|archive-date=28 August 2015}}</ref> He made his league debut in his second spell three days later, starting and being [[Penalty card#Yellow card|booked]] in a 0–0 home draw against [[Sporting de Gijón]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2015/08/29/radio_san_sebastian/1440877700_341866.html|title=Ni con Illarramendi|trans-title=Not even with Illarramendi|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|first=Roberto|last=Ramajo|language=es|date=29 August 2015|access-date=31 August 2015}}</ref> He recorded his first goal for the team in his second spell on 25 October, in a 4–0 win at [[Levante UD]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/liga-bbva/levante-0-4-real-sociedad-david-moyes-morale-boost-4616897|title=Levante 0–4 Real Sociedad: David Moyes' morale boost|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|date=25 October 2015|access-date=25 October 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304123222/http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/liga-bbva/levante-0-4-real-sociedad-david-moyes-morale-boost-4616897|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

In the [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17 campaign]], Illarramendi had the second-highest number of interceptions across Europe's five major leagues behind only [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s [[N'Golo Kante]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/10803609/how-chelseas-ngolo-kante-compares-to-europes-best-midfielders|title=How Chelsea's N'Golo Kante compares to Europe's best midfielders|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Martin|last=Laurence|date=16 March 2017|access-date=18 March 2017}}</ref> However, he was also noted for his poor disciplinary record, having racked up ten yellow cards by March 2017 including one in each of his four previous games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-sociedad/20170314/42857596980/la-fiebre-amarilla-de-asier-illarramendi.html|title=La fiebre amarilla de Asier Illarramendi|trans-title=Asier Illarramendi's yellow fever|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Ángel|last=López|language=es|date=14 March 2017|access-date=18 March 2017}}</ref>

Illarramendi scored a career-best seven goals in [[2017–18 La Liga|2017–18]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-sociedad/20200826/483038110709/cinco-anos-de-mas-a-menos.html|title=Cinco años de más a menos|trans-title=Five years going from more to less|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Xabier|last=Isasa|language=es|date=26 August 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> including braces in home and away victories over [[Deportivo de La Coruña]]. He had already exceeded his professional output for his whole career by February with his fifth goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-sociedad/2018/02/05/5a787f37268e3ed1608b4620.html|title=El Illarramendi con más gol|trans-title=The most-scoring Illarramendi|newspaper=Marca|first=Óscar|last=Badallo|language=es|date=5 February 2018|access-date=9 May 2020}}</ref>

On 30 August 2019, Illarramendi suffered a broken [[fibula]] in a [[Basque derby]] match against [[Athletic Bilbao]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/08/31/5d6a5d3e46163f13388b4616.html|title=Illarramendi to have surgery on broken fibula and faces two months out|newspaper=Marca|first1=Óscar|last1=Badallo|first2=Billy|last2=Munday|date=31 August 2019|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> it was presumed the injury would keep him out for a few months, but it was found he required surgery to his shin and ankle ligaments, and he did not feature again prior to [[2019–20 La Liga|the season]] being halted in March 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]. The delay seemed to have given him time to return before its conclusion, but in June 2020 he suffered a further muscle injury on the training ground, and made no further appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/illarramendi-s-season-expected-to-be-over-after-real-sociedad-training-injury/ar-BB15zrwD?li=BBoPWjP|title=Illarramendi's season expected to be over after Real Sociedad training injury|publisher=[[MSN]]|first=Tom|last=Webber|date=16 June 2020|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref>

On 24 May 2023, it was announced that [[Captain (association football)|captain]] Illarramendi would leave the [[Anoeta Stadium]] on 30 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-espana.net/2023/05/24/real-sociedad-captain-to-leave-at-the-end-of-the-season|title=Real Sociedad captain to leave at the end of the season|publisher=Football España|first=Ruairidh|last=Barlow|date=24 May 2023|access-date=25 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/illarramendi-adios-a-la-real-n/|title=Illarramendi deja la Real Sociedad: "Me voy en paz, lo he dado todo"|trans-title=Illarramendi leaves Real Sociedad: "I leave in peace, I have given everything"|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Roberto|last=Ramajo|language=es|date=24 May 2023|access-date=16 June 2023}}</ref>

===FC Dallas===
On 3 August 2023, Illarramendi signed with [[Major League Soccer]] club [[FC Dallas]] on a deal until the end of [[2023 Major League Soccer season|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcdallas.com/news/fc-dallas-acquires-free-agent-midfielder-asier-illarramendi|title=FC Dallas acquires free agent midfielder Asier Illarramendi|publisher=FC Dallas|date=3 August 2023|access-date=3 August 2023}}</ref> He finished his [[2024 Major League Soccer season|first full campaign]] with 25 games (22 starts) and two goals; additionally, he had a 90% passing rate and recovered the ball 157 times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bigdsoccer.com/2024-fc-dallas-player-recaps-asier-illarramendi/|title=2024 FC Dallas Player Recaps: Asier Illarramendi|publisher=Big D Soccer|first=Drew|last=Epperley|date=21 October 2024|access-date=1 October 2025}}</ref>

Illarramendi was not retained for the [[2025 Major League Soccer season|2025 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-sociedad/20241212/1002369920/dallas-protege-illarramendi.html|title=Dallas no protege a Illarramendi|trans-title=Dallas do not protect Illarramendi|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Unai|last=Valverde|language=es|date=12 December 2024|access-date=1 October 2025}}</ref>

===Kitchee===
Illarramendi moved countries again on 10 September 2025, with the 35-year-old joining [[Hong Kong Premier League]]'s [[Kitchee SC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1822221-20250910.htm|title=Former Real Madrid star Illarramendi joins Kitchee|publisher=[[RTHK]]|date=10 September 2025|access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://hk.on.cc/hk/bkn/cnt/sport/20250910/bkn-20250910201258094-0910_00882_001.html|title=港超聯　前皇馬中場伊拿拉文迪加盟傑志|trans-title=Hong Kong Premier League: Former Real Madrid midfielder Illarramendi joins Kitchee|publisher=HK01|language=zh|date=10 September 2025|access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Illarramendi helped [[Spain national under-17 football team|Spain]] to reach the final of the [[2007 FIFA U-17 World Cup]], featuring in all games but one. He missed one of the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalties]] in the final [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shootout]], which allowed [[Nigeria national under-17 football team|Nigeria]] to lift the trophy.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2007/09/09/actualidad/1189322518_850215.html|title=España pierde la final del Mundial sub-17 ante Nigeria en la tanda de penalties|trans-title=Spain lose under-17 World Cup final to Nigeria on penalties|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=9 September 2007|access-date=2 May 2023}}</ref>

Illarramendi played 16 times for [[Spain national under-21 football team|the under-21s]] in two years. He represented them at the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2013 UEFA European Championship]] in Israel, being first choice as the nation won the competition and being selected in the team of the tournament.<ref name=U21>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0252-0cd3add5c6c6-33fdf8fdc07a-1000--thiago-leads-all-star-squad-dominated-by-spain/|title=Thiago leads all-star squad dominated by Spain|publisher=UEFA|first=Kevin|last=Ashby|date=21 June 2013|access-date=8 July 2013}}</ref>

Manager [[Julen Lopetegui]] first called up Illarramendi for the [[Spain national football team|senior side]] in March 2017, ahead of a [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifier]] against [[Israel national football team|Israel]] and a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] with [[France national football team|France]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/03/17/football/1489747654_939989.html|title=Iker Casillas out of Spain squad, Deulofeu and Illarramendi in|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Joaquín|last=Maroto|date=17 March 2017|access-date=18 March 2017}}</ref> Additionally, he played for the [[Basque Country national football team|Basque XI]] from 2013 onwards, opening a 3–1 win over [[FIFA]] member [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]] on 30 December 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eitb.eus/es/deportes/futbol/detalle/4569100/la-euskal-selekzioa-derrota-tunez-se-toma-revancha-2011/|title=La Euskal Selekzioa derrota a Túnez y se toma la revancha de 2011|trans-title=The Basque team defeat Tunisia and avenge 2011|publisher=[[EITB]]|language=es|date=30 December 2016|access-date=18 March 2017}}</ref>

Illarramendi made his debut for Spain on 7 June 2017, playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–2 friendly draw with [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] in [[Murcia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/seleccion/2017/06/07/5938581b268e3e6b618b4674.html|title=Illarramendi por fin debuta con España|trans-title=Illarramendi finally makes Spain debut|newspaper=Marca|first=Javier|last=Estepa|language=es|date=7 June 2017|access-date=7 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/amistosos_seleccion/4/spa_col/|title=Morata no pierde el tiempo|trans-title=Morata does not waste time|newspaper=Marca|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=7 June 2017|access-date=7 June 2017}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 9 October that year, netting the game's only in [[Israel national football team|Israel]] for the World Cup qualifying campaign.<ref name=Wonder>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/clasificacion_mundial/2016_17/grupo_g/jornada_10/isr_spa/|title=Un golazo de Illarra premia a España|trans-title=Illarra wonder goal rewards Spain|newspaper=Marca|first=Enrique|last=Ortego|language=es|date=9 October 2017|access-date=9 October 2017}}</ref>
